w_339c63cbd3: remaining cells appear distinctly larger, more spread/flattened with jagged periphery and prominent peripheral F-actin (red) and longer major axis.
w_339c63cbd3: nuclei (blue) on average larger, with occasional notably large nuclei; shape remains round/oval, smooth contour, no obvious fragmentation.

w_75056a5b47 3uM fields f_1de09e4ea67f,f_67fac3e5a86a: confluence high but nuclei clearly larger than DMSO, many cells with enlarged pale-blue nuclei; cells also modestly larger, more spread than DMSO.

Beta-tubulin (green) network retained in all treated fields: no loss, no thick bundles, no monopolar rosettes. F-actin (red) not lost; if anything peripheral cortical actin more conspicuous. No cell rounding/shrinkage.

No obvious increase in bright condensed mitotic figures vs DMSO; DMSO shows several bright DAPI mitoses, treated show similar or fewer. No multinucleated clusters clearly resolved at this composite resolution.
DAPI brightness/DNA content increase and act/tub ratio increase reported by features not reliably quantifiable by eye in composite at fixed contrast; requires grayscale channels.

DNA damage/DNA replication can also enlarge cells but less specific; image lacks focal DNA-damage or replication-stress hallmark; actin/microtubule phenotype argues against Actin disruptors, Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors.

reflection.text:
Unblinded as cisplatin - DNA inhibitor / DNA damage, verdict correct (protocol 3/4 wells NSC DNA damage). My call DNA damage p=0.62 was directionally correct and review-approved, though mildly optimistic.

What got it right:
- Acquisition strategy: after checking 8 doses/4 wells (e1), sampling the full 0.3-30 uM window captured the true window. Wells w_be5255b779 (0.3uM), w_75056a5b47 (3uM) and w_339c63cbd3 (10uM) all showed consistent enlargement: cell_area z=+3.8 to +10.5 and nuc_area z=+3.6 to +5.8 (e3,e4,e5). This plus cell_count z=-3.0 to -7.0 and rho=-0.80 for cell_count (e9) matches DNA-damage G2 arrest / polyploid enlargement phenotype. Literature returned supports this: cisplatin DNA crosslink mechanism PMID 25058905, PMID 36368406, PMID 38520407 and PMID 32132710; and carcinogen-induced nuclear enlargement PMID 20693082 and polyploid giant cell formation PMID 41955234.
- Comparison: compare_to_reference_atlas (e6) NSC vote 3/4 DNA damage correctly outweighed k-neighbour frequency 6/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors. Protocol confirms 1-NN per well majority vote 3/4 DNA damage, summed similarity 1.205 vs 1 vote Microtubule stabilizers 0.464. I weighted NSC correctly (e15: DNA damage 0.62 vs Aurora 0.22).
- I correctly down-weighted non-significant dose_response: all n=4 tests p>=0.2 - cell_area rho=-0.20 p0.8 (e7), nuc_area rho=-0.40 p0.6 (e8), frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.40 p0.6 (e10), nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.80 p0.2 (e11) - so did not chase the apparent negative trend from including the toxic well.

What misled / what I missed:
- Highest dose w_060cb9f994 30uM (e2): 167 cells, nuc_form_factor z=-11.9, cell_count z=-11.6, act_glcm_contrast z=+11.2. Acquiring the max dose first as planned maximized toxicity artifact. It voted Microtubule stabilizers similarity 0.464 alone, driving cell_area/nuc_area dose_response non-monotonic and nuc_dna_integrated decrease. I correctly called it toxic outlier in rationale but still spent 1/4 budget on it, leaving all key doses single-replicate with no power to reach p<0.2.
- Contradictory second classifier: k-neighbour 6/10 Aurora (e6) + describe_phenotype candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors (e14) + frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 p0.2 (e12) kept Aurora alive at 0.22. I noted contradicting e12/e13 for Aurora but review was right that 0.62 was optimistic; Aurora remains credible given atlas neighbours and visual density loss.
- I did not acquire replicates at 0.3-10uM where phenotype was clean; with 0/4 wells left I could not test reproducibility or exclude the 30uM toxic regime from dose_response. The identity check mismatch (CID 5702198 vs BBBC021 CID 2767) was correctly ignored for MOA but flagged structure uncertainty.

Lesson: For DNA damage vs Aurora, avoid 30uM cytotoxic ceiling; reserve wells for duplicate 1-10uM to make dose_response and multinucleate/mitotic proxies informative, and rely on NSC 1-NN majority vote over k-NN frequency and single-field microscopy impression. Next experiment as proposed: gamma-H2AX + cell-cycle PI across 0.3-10uM with reference DNA damage control.
